title: Hero Text That Bursts Into Dust Then Settles on Hover | vitalii.no
description:
How a homepage hero title went from a permanently-visible dust smudge to a clean burst effect that only appears on hover.

The first version of this effect worked on a single tile and left its particles sitting as a faint, permanently visible mound at rest — even when nothing was hovered. A second attempt made it work across every tile, but the grid re-laying itself out under the cursor could make the hover state blink null for a single frame, restarting the whole animation mid-flight.

A React component built on the Canvas API now samples the pixels of the hero text itself instead of drawing a resting mound, so at rest it is just plain text — nothing is drawn on the canvas at all. On hover those pixels burst into a drifting cloud, capped at 7,000 grains, and settle into the hovered tile's title in that section's own neon colour. Leaving is debounced by 160 milliseconds specifically so a one-frame relayout glitch can't restart the burst, and the simulation runs on fixed 60Hz substeps so the flight takes the same time regardless of the browser's actual frame rate.

Two small numbers — a 160ms debounce and a 7,000-grain cap — turned a single-tile prototype with a visible resting mound into an effect that works cleanly across every tile without ever restarting itself.
